title: x to the 8th in 3 ops
starter:
%x = param 0 dtype=i32
# correct, but 7 ops. Get it to 3.
%a1 = mul %x %x
%a2 = mul %a1 %x
%a3 = mul %a2 %x
%a4 = mul %a3 %x
%a5 = mul %a4 %x
%a6 = mul %a5 %x
%out = mul %a6 %x
hints: Square, then square the result, then square again. Each step is one `mul` whose two operands are the same node.
`mul %a %a` is allowed: a node can be used twice. That reuse is the whole trick.

answer.explain: Repeated squaring computes x^2, x^4, x^8 with three `mul`s by reusing each result as both operands. i32 multiplication wraps, but it is still associative and commutative mod 2^32, so the regrouping gives exactly the same bits as seven multiplies, including the wraparound cases.
